name: Rochelle Jordan
label: Empire
lede: A YouTube cover singer who got ten DMs from a Virginia Beach producer, lost seven years to a bad deal, and came back with a 17-track house album that landed at No. 25 on Pitchfork's 2025 list.

eras.title: Ten DMs from Virginia Beach
eras.text: A kid raised near Toronto on her brother's gospel, house and jungle tapes posts R&B covers online and gets found by a producer who will not stop messaging her. The partnership that starts here is still running.

years.h: Born in High Wycombe, raised outside Toronto
years.p: Rochelle Jordan is born to Jamaican parents in England and moves to Wheatley, Ontario at 4. She is diagnosed with sickle cell anemia at 2.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, her father was a musician, and frequent hospital stays marked her childhood. The FADER adds that she is the youngest of three, with two older brothers seven and ten years her senior.

Her brother Junior's tastes shaped her ears: gospel, house, drum and bass and jungle. She has cited UK rave culture, from visits to family in London, as another root.

years.cap: Rochelle Jordan and KLSH, the partnership behind every release. Photo needed.
years.src: The FADER · Paste · RANGE · Wikipedia: Rochelle Jordan · NME
years.h: A Virginia Beach producer sends her ten DMs in a row
years.p: [[KLSH|3bf71d97-a5f8-4e74-bca4-fe52059f4c16]] finds her R&B covers on YouTube and keeps messaging until she answers. He is still executive producer on everything she releases.
years.xp:
The FADER reports KLSH sent ten consecutive direct messages. Paste says they connected over a MySpace beat called "Neptune", and RANGE reports he flew her to Los Angeles for sessions. Paste dates her move to LA to age 19. Their first release together was the 2010 mixtape Alien Phase.

Wikipedia has her uploading cover versions at 16, inspired by Justin Bieber's YouTube start; NME puts her first singing videos at 19. Sources differ on the age.

eras.title: Namechecked, then blog-famous
eras.text: Three mixtapes in two years, a Drake mention, a Childish Gambino cut, and a debut album made in a Los Angeles bedroom. Her leftfield R&B gets the Aaliyah comparisons before the sound has a name.

years.h: Drake namechecks her on "Club Paradise"; Rojo and Origins drop
years.p: [[Drake|9fff2f8a-21e6-47de-a2b8-7f449929d43f]] mentions her by name the same year she puts out two mixtapes, Rojo and Origins.
years.xp: Paste reports she later worked out what the mention meant: her habit of stripping rap beats down to bare bones in R&B remixes, including a "Marvin's Room" remix Drake reportedly liked.

years.h: Pressure puts a trap-soul spin on it
years.p: Her third mixtape is covered by Now Toronto in August 2012 under the title "P R E S S U R E".
years.xp: Paste describes the project as trap soul.

years.h: Childish Gambino puts her on "Telegraph Ave."
years.p: [[Childish Gambino|7fb57fba-a6ef-44c2-abab-2fa3bdee607e]] brings her in for a track on Because the Internet.
years.xp: NME lists the Gambino collaboration alongside the Drake mention as the early signals that the blogs were not the ceiling.

years.h: 1021, the debut, recorded in her LA bedroom
years.p: Her first album is named for her birthday, October 21. "Lowkey" and "Follow Me" are written in this period and stay her calling cards.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she recorded it in her Los Angeles bedroom. Vice ran a feature on her that November headlined "Rochelle Jordan is Making R&B That Brings the Whole World to Your Bedroom". In 2015, YouKnowIGotSoul interviewed her about the Toronto sound and the Aaliyah comparisons.

Paste dates "Follow Me" and "Lowkey" to 2014. "Lowkey" would be a TikTok hit a decade later.

eras.title: The wall
eras.text: The good reviews do not turn into a career. A contract she calls toxic and a depression she was managing alongside sickle cell swallow almost seven years.

years.big: "The wall of this dynamic between me and this person"
q: The wall of this dynamic between me and this person.
years.src: Paste · Wikipedia: Play with the Changes · The Guardian
years.h: Seven years inside a bad deal
years.p: After 1021 she signs what she later calls a "toxic" record deal. Wikipedia says the pressure and her health fed a near-seven-year silence.
years.xp:
Paste reports she spent years with an A&R representative she trusted, and that she describes the fear built up around that relationship as something she had to break down. She ended it near the end of the 2010s and went independent.

The Guardian's 2021 interview carried her line as its headline: "I had to learn to not let anybody strangle or suffocate my career again."

years.h: TOKiMONSTA signs her to Young Art
years.p: [[TOKiMONSTA|96f6ec97-998c-4991-b836-7b71feb3ca6f]]'s label gives her a home and ends the silence that followed 1021.

eras.title: Back on her own terms
eras.text: Seven years after her debut, she returns with a club record about depression, longing and police brutality, and critics treat it as a comeback that beat the odds.

years.src: Wikipedia: Play with the Changes · Bandcamp Daily · The Culture Crypt
years.h: Play with the Changes ends the silence
years.p: Her second album, on Young Art, is built on UK garage, drum and bass, house and jungle. It lands at 86 on Metacritic.
years.xp:
KLSH is the main producer, with [[Machinedrum|d1785218-d8f4-4a83-a33d-8cf737eef918]] mixing and co-producing, plus [[Jimmy Edgar|fa263cb3-205f-4a7f-91e1-94e3df52abe8]], Alix Perez and Sepalcure. Farrah Fawx guests on "Broken Steel". Bandcamp Daily notes she recorded it in her bedroom, like her earlier records.

Wikipedia lists it on year-end lists at Exclaim!, Clash and PopMatters (No. 10), and on the Polaris Music Prize long list. A remix edition featured Kaytranada, Sango, KLSH and LSDXOXO, per The Culture Crypt.

eras.title: Through the wall
eras.text: A TikTok resurrection of a decade-old song, a move to Empire, and a 17-track house album that ends up on year-end lists.

years.h: "Lowkey" goes viral on TikTok, ten years late
years.p: The 2014 song from 1021 takes off, and The Culture Crypt puts it near 30 million streams by 2024.
years.xp: NME dates the TikTok surge to 2024. The same year she appears on [[Kelela|045494aa-e913-4e62-bf4e-dcc276e0075a]]'s RAVE:N, The Remixes and [[Kaytranada|e56aee57-d90e-40cf-a70d-beb70f6f3c69]]'s TIMELESS, per The Culture Crypt.

years.p: The independent label takes her on, and its president Tina Davis calls her the most important piece of its dance roster, per The FADER.
"Crave" goes out May 30, "TTW" on July 11, "Doing It Too" on August 8 and "Sweet Sensation" on September 12.

years.src: Album of the Year · Metacritic · Beatportal · Paste · Wikipedia: Through the Wall · Pop Crave
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and ranked it No. 25 of 2025. Metacritic has it at 90 from five critics.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and Album of the Year list it as a September 26, 2025 release on Empire. Album of the Year records Pitchfork's 83 (Gio Santiago), calling it a sleek, perfectly executed club record. Metacritic's Line of Best Fit and AllMusic each gave 90, Consequence and Pitchfork 83.

KLSH is executive producer. Beatportal credits Kaytranada on "The Boy", Jimmy Edgar on "Bite the Bait" and [[DāM-FunK|6d6d607e-679a-4cdc-a7a0-35e2abe06619]] on "Sweet Sensation", with Byron the Aquarius, Hamdi and MPH also on the list. Paste has Initial Talk and Terry Hunter as well.

years.src: Album of the Year · Pop Crave · Wikipedia: Through the Wall · The FADER
years.h: Year-end lists: The FADER No. 2, Pitchfork No. 25
years.p: Album of the Year logs The FADER at No. 2 and Pitchfork at No. 25, and Wikipedia adds CBC's best Canadian albums at No. 3.
years.xp: Pop Crave posted Pitchfork's placement, with the 8.3 score, on December 5, 2025. The FADER followed with a March 2026 cover story on her slow burn.

years.h: A sold-out fall run becomes a 2026 world tour
years.p: North American dates in autumn 2025 sell out, then she adds Europe in February 2026 and North America in March and April.

years.h: Through the Wall makes the 2026 Polaris long list
years.p: "The Boy" also lands on the SOCAN Polaris Song Prize long list.
years.xp: Wikipedia cites Exclaim!'s June 11, 2026 long-list report and CBC Music's June 24 song-prize list.
